claims.title: Supplier paperwork may be intercepted while crossing from suppliers to the vendor portal
claims.description: `flow:entity:supplier>process:supplier-portal>upload-documents` carries supplier staff contact details and compliance documents tagged `pii` and `business-critical-data` across the public-internet-to-vendor-platform boundary, but its `protocol` and `encryption_in_transit` are unknown. If transport protection is absent or ineffective, an on-path observer reads the uploaded documents and contact details in transit. The crossing depends on the model's inferred placement of `entity:supplier`, so the transport posture and supplier access path must be verified. The captured personal and business information can then be used to target suppliers and identify documents held in `store:document-store`.

severity.justification: Likelihood is high, conditional on the unknown transport controls, because `flow:entity:supplier>process:supplier-portal>upload-documents` crosses from `boundary:public-internet` and any supplier-facing route can be probed by external attackers. Impact is medium because the flow is tagged `pii` and `business-critical-data`, exposing supplier staff details and compliance records.

mitigations.summary: Verify and require encrypted supplier uploads
mitigations.detail: Set a verified HTTPS/TLS 1.2+ transport posture for `flow:entity:supplier>process:supplier-portal>upload-documents`, with modern certificate validation and HSTS.

mitigations.summary: Minimize data sent with each upload
mitigations.detail: Keep contact details and other unnecessary metadata out of upload requests; use opaque document references where the portal can resolve metadata server-side.

claims.title: Category-manager review traffic may expose supplier documents across the corporate-to-vendor boundary
claims.description: `flow:entity:category-manager>process:supplier-portal>review-documents` crosses from `boundary:corporate-network` to `boundary:vendor-platform` and has unknown `protocol`, `authentication`, and `encryption_in_transit`. If its transport protection is absent or ineffective, an attacker able to observe that inter-zone route can intercept document-review content, approval decisions, and associated supplier information. Those records identify which documents and suppliers are in `store:document-store`, enabling targeted social engineering or later attempts to obtain the underlying paperwork.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium, conditional on unknown transport controls, because an attacker needs a position on the corporate-network-to-vendor-platform route rather than merely public access. Impact is medium because the flow carries supplier review material tagged `pii` and `business-critical-data`.

mitigations.summary: Require verified TLS for manager portal sessions
mitigations.detail: Require TLS 1.2+ with certificate validation for `flow:entity:category-manager>process:supplier-portal>review-documents`; document the protocol and cipher requirements in the vendor security agreement.

mitigations.summary: Restrict review content to the portal session
mitigations.detail: Avoid putting supplier details or approval information into URLs and minimize the document fields returned to category-manager views.

claims.title: Uploaded documents may be readable on the portal-to-document-store path
claims.description: `flow:process:supplier-portal>store:document-store>store-documents` transfers uploaded compliance documents tagged `pii` and `business-critical-data`, but its `protocol`, `authentication`, and `encryption_in_transit` are unknown. If the vendor's internal storage path is not encrypted, an attacker with an observation position in the vendor platform can intercept documents as the portal stores them. The captured content identifies sensitive supplier records subsequently retained by `store:document-store` and can support targeted disclosure attempts against that store.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low, conditional on the unknown transport controls, because interception requires a foothold or observation point inside `boundary:vendor-platform`. Impact is medium because the flow transfers documents tagged `pii` and `business-critical-data`.

mitigations.summary: Obtain and enforce vendor internal-transport assurances
mitigations.detail: Require the vendor to verify encrypted service-to-storage transport for `flow:process:supplier-portal>store:document-store>store-documents`, preferably with mutually authenticated TLS.

mitigations.summary: Reduce document exposure during storage
mitigations.detail: Encrypt sensitive document payloads before storage where feasible and ensure portal-to-store telemetry does not capture document bodies or contact details.

claims.title: Nightly supplier extracts may be intercepted while moving from the vendor into the landing bucket
claims.description: `flow:entity:portal-vendor>store:landing-bucket>push-nightly-extract` crosses from `boundary:vendor-platform` to `boundary:cloud-account` carrying the nightly supplier data extract tagged `pii` and `business-critical-data`, while its protocol, authentication, and encryption in transit are unknown. If the end-to-end transport protection is absent or ineffective, an attacker on this inter-environment route can intercept the full nightly extract. The extract is then available outside the intended ingestion path and can be used to identify or target the supplier records written later to `store:supplier-database`.

quotes.text:
We were told the nightly extract is encrypted end to end. The runbook for the
landing bucket says the file arrives as a plain CSV and is picked up as-is.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because `flow:entity:portal-vendor>store:landing-bucket>push-nightly-extract` is a cross-boundary transfer with unverified protocol and transport encryption, but interception still requires an on-path position. Impact is medium because one intercepted extract contains `pii` and `business-critical-data` for the nightly supplier dataset.

mitigations.summary: Use a verified encrypted vendor-to-bucket transfer
mitigations.detail: Require a documented protocol such as mutually authenticated TLS or a managed private transfer mechanism for `flow:entity:portal-vendor>store:landing-bucket>push-nightly-extract`, with certificate and endpoint ownership verification.

mitigations.summary: Encrypt the extract as a file before transfer
mitigations.detail: Have the vendor encrypt each extract to a customer-controlled recipient key before upload, so transport or bucket exposure alone does not reveal its contents.

claims.title: The supplier master service may receive the nightly extract over an unverified channel
claims.description: `flow:process:supplier-master-service>store:landing-bucket>load-extract` is a read path for the nightly supplier extract and has unknown protocol, authentication, and `encryption_in_transit`. If this internal channel lacks effective transport encryption, an attacker with a foothold on the cloud-account path can intercept the extract while `process:supplier-master-service` loads it from `store:landing-bucket`. The captured data can be correlated with the supplier records the service later writes to `store:supplier-database`.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low, conditional on unknown controls, because intercepting the non-crossing `flow:process:supplier-master-service>store:landing-bucket>load-extract` requires a prior observation position in `boundary:cloud-account`. Impact is medium because the extract is tagged `pii` and `business-critical-data`.

mitigations.summary: Encrypt and authenticate the service-to-bucket read path
mitigations.detail: Require TLS 1.2+ or the cloud provider's authenticated private endpoint mechanism for `flow:process:supplier-master-service>store:landing-bucket>load-extract` and record the verified setting.

mitigations.summary: Use a narrowly scoped workload identity
mitigations.detail: Give `process:supplier-master-service` a dedicated, short-lived identity limited to reading the specific expected extract object.

claims.title: Supplier records may be exposed on the service-to-database write path
claims.description: `flow:process:supplier-master-service>store:supplier-database>write-supplier-records` carries supplier records tagged `pii` and `business-critical-data`, but its protocol, authentication, and encryption in transit are unknown. If encryption is not effective, an attacker observing this cloud-account path can intercept records while `process:supplier-master-service` writes them into `store:supplier-database`. The captured records disclose the same supplier information later concentrated in the database and can enable targeted fraud or social engineering against affected suppliers.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low, conditional on unknown transport controls, because an attacker must first obtain an observation position on the internal cloud-account path. Impact is medium because the written supplier records are tagged `pii` and `business-critical-data`.

mitigations.summary: Require encrypted database connections
mitigations.detail: Configure `flow:process:supplier-master-service>store:supplier-database>write-supplier-records` to use TLS with server certificate validation, and preferably mutual authentication for the service identity.

mitigations.summary: Limit transmitted fields
mitigations.detail: Transmit only the supplier-record fields required for loading and avoid carrying unneeded contact or document metadata to the database.

claims.title: A copied document-store volume may disclose supplier paperwork if encryption at rest is absent
claims.description: `store:document-store` retains uploaded compliance documents and is tagged `pii` and `business-critical-data`, but its `data_classification` and `encryption_at_rest` are unknown. If the unknown at-rest setting resolves to no effective encryption, a person who obtains its storage media or an operational copy can read the documents without using `process:supplier-portal` or the portal's normal authentication path. This disclosure provides supplier contact details and compliance information that can enable targeted attacks against suppliers and category-manager review workflows. This is conditional on the unverified at-rest control, not an assertion that the vendor store is unencrypted.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional on `unknown:store:document-store:encryption_at_rest`: a storage or operational copy must be obtained, but that bypasses the portal access path if encryption is absent. Impact is medium because the store holds documents tagged `pii` and `business-critical-data`.

mitigations.summary: Verify encryption at rest for vendor-held documents
mitigations.detail: Obtain evidence that `store:document-store` uses encryption at rest with managed keys and that the protection covers backups, snapshots, exports, and decommissioned media.

mitigations.summary: Restrict access to document copies and keys
mitigations.detail: Require least-privilege operational access, separate key-use permissions from storage-read permissions, and audit export or snapshot operations.

claims.title: A copied landing-bucket object may disclose the nightly supplier extract if at-rest encryption is absent
claims.description: `store:landing-bucket` holds the nightly supplier data extract and is tagged `pii` and `business-critical-data`, but its `data_classification` and `encryption_at_rest` are unknown. If at-rest encryption is absent or ineffective, an attacker who obtains a bucket object, storage copy, backup, or snapshot can read the complete extract without authenticating through `process:supplier-master-service`. The extract can then be correlated with records in `store:supplier-database`, extending the disclosure beyond a single supplier interaction. This draft is conditional on the unresolved encryption-at-rest attribute.

quotes.text:
The runbook for the
landing bucket says the file arrives as a plain CSV and is picked up as-is.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional on `unknown:store:landing-bucket:encryption_at_rest`, because obtaining an operational copy is a prerequisite but such a copy bypasses application controls if it is not encrypted. Impact is medium because the bucket contains a nightly extract tagged `pii` and `business-critical-data`.

mitigations.summary: Encrypt landing-bucket objects and operational copies
mitigations.detail: Enable and verify managed-key or customer-managed-key encryption for `store:landing-bucket`, including versioned objects, backups, snapshots, and exports.

mitigations.summary: Encrypt the extract before it reaches the bucket
mitigations.detail: Require application-level encryption of each vendor extract to a customer-controlled key so a copied bucket object remains unreadable.

claims.title: A copied supplier-database volume may reveal supplier records if encryption at rest is absent
claims.description: `store:supplier-database` stores supplier records tagged `pii` and `business-critical-data`, while both its data classification and `encryption_at_rest` are unknown. If storage encryption is absent or ineffective, an attacker who acquires a database volume, backup, snapshot, or other storage-layer copy can read the supplier corpus without needing the normal service path from `process:supplier-master-service`. The disclosed records can be combined with the nightly extract in `store:landing-bucket` to profile suppliers and their staff. This is a conditional storage-copy threat, not a claim that encryption is absent.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional on `unknown:store:supplier-database:encryption_at_rest`: the attacker must obtain a storage-layer copy, but absent encryption that copy can be read independently of the application. Impact is medium because the database holds supplier records tagged `pii` and `business-critical-data`.

mitigations.summary: Enforce database encryption at rest across copies
mitigations.detail: Establish and record the encryption-at-rest posture of `store:supplier-database`; require managed-key encryption for the primary database, backups, snapshots, replicas, and exported dumps.

mitigations.summary: Separate storage access from key use
mitigations.detail: Limit database backup and export permissions, use separate key-use roles, and alert on snapshot, restore, and export activity.

claims.title: Code running in the supplier master service can read the full landing extract through its reader path
claims.description: `process:supplier-master-service` loads the nightly extract from `store:landing-bucket` through the read flow `flow:process:supplier-master-service>store:landing-bucket>load-extract`. An attacker who runs code in that service can use its established reader path to obtain the full extract, including data tagged `pii` and `business-critical-data`; encryption at rest would not prevent a read served to an authorized workload. The flow's authentication is unknown, so the service identity, bucket scope, and whether it can read more than the expected object must be verified. The acquired extract can then be correlated with the supplier records the service writes to `store:supplier-database`.

quotes.text:
Our supplier master service loads that file and writes the
records into the supplier database.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low because the attacker must first run code in `process:supplier-master-service` and the model states no exposed compromise path. Impact is medium because its established read flow obtains the landing extract tagged `pii` and `business-critical-data`.

mitigations.summary: Limit the service identity to one expected object
mitigations.detail: Use a dedicated short-lived workload identity for `process:supplier-master-service` that can read only the expected landing-bucket prefix and cannot list, export, or read unrelated objects.

mitigations.summary: Detect unexpected extract reads
mitigations.detail: Log and alert on bucket reads by the supplier-master identity that occur outside the nightly job, exceed expected object size, or access unexpected object versions.
